wired.why: the absence of the operator's decision, said as an absence: a wiring that names nothing is not a reader that reads nothing
a name the caravan does not know is not a promise: there is nothing to read against it, whatever the name looks like
the defect the file is for: a model whose name says vision and whose facts say `text` is a text model. The promise is read from `ModelKind`, never from the name
the absence of a promise, kept apart from a promise that the model cannot read: facts that name no inputs are the operator's absence of a named work
the negative case: the only state that reads, and the part goes to it as a caption
the word is the part's own word, not the word this rule decides: the same reader is a reader for `image` and not one for `audio`
a pool cannot be its own reader: the caption would come from the row that cannot read the part, so this is answered before the promise is read, whatever the facts say
the negative case for the same rule: a self-naming is answered as itself even when the promise would answer `reads`, because it is not a question of what the model takes

the negative case for where the rule is asked from: the board's row names no pool, so a name there cannot be the board itself, and `itself` cannot answer. The same name answers `itself` for a request, whose pool is named — the answer is the pool, not the name
the absence named at the entry: `EntryModels::wired` answers `Nothing` for an empty name, so a wiring to nothing never becomes a reader with an empty name

caption.why: the reader's words stay words: a `<` in a caption must not end the envelope early, which is how a caption turns into an instruction

caption.why: the attributes are escaped as the text is: a name read from a config file is not trusted to be a name

caption.why: the absence, said as an absence: an empty caption is an empty caption, and nothing here turns an empty answer into a caption

key.why: the three fields the cache tells captions apart by, kept as fields: the part is named by the bytes it came as, and this module never hashes a picture
the defect a joined key has: a reader whose name holds the separator would share a key with a different reader, which is the one thing a cache must never do
the same key twice is the same key: it is built from the fields, so two calls that mean the same caption cannot come out different

words.message: The model `gemma` does not take image, and no reader is wired for it. Message 1 part 1: image. Send the request to a model that takes image, or wire a reader on Routing.
words.why: the words come from the answer the rule gave, not from a state named by hand, and the numbers are the client's own: the message and the part as it sent them

words.message: The reader wired for `gemma` names `qwen3-vl-8b-instruct`, which does not take image. Message 1 part 1: image. The wiring names a model that cannot read what the request carries.
words.why: "wire a reader" is wrong advice here, and the words say so: a reader is already wired, and it cannot read — the advice would send the operator to wire the same text model again

words.message: The reader wired for `gemma` names `qwen3-vl-8b-instruct` and says nothing of what it takes. Message 1 part 1: image. Its promise is not said, so nothing was read.
words.why: the absence of a promise is not a promise that the model cannot read, so it gets its own words and its own code: a refusal that says "does not take image" here would state a fact the caravan does not have

words.message: The reader wired for `gemma` names `qwen-vl`, which the caravan does not know. Message 1 part 1: image. A wiring that cannot be checked is not a path that reads.
words.why: a name read out of a config file is not a reader until the caravan knows it: the words say which name cannot be checked, because a name is the one thing this rule must not read a capability from

words.message: The reader wired for `gemma` names `gemma`, the pool the wiring is for. Message 1 part 1: image. A pool cannot be its own reader: the caption would come from the row that cannot read it.
words.why: one answer, one code, whichever path asked it: the board that saves a name and the entry that reads a request read the same `EntryRefusal::wiring`, so a self-naming cannot be refused with two different sentences
the negative case: a wiring that reads the word is not refused, and the refusal function answers `None` for it. A table of only refusals cannot tell a rule from a guess
the negative case for the row: a row that reads the picture is never given a caption, and the part goes to it as it came

words.message: The model `gemma` does not take image, and no reader is wired for it. Message 1 part 2: image. Send the request to a model that takes image, or wire a reader on Routing.
words.why: the refusal names the part the classifier named, not the one a loose word match would have picked: `image_text` is a picture, and the text part before it is not refused
the absence of a promise is not refused by this rule: a row that says nothing of itself is the operator's to name on the board, and an answer that is not a refusal answers `None`

names.why: the door checks a name against the facts the reading has about it: a subscription's facts say it takes image, so this writes. On the live board the same name was refused with `media_reader_unknown` on 2026-11-06, because the reading the door asked from held the pools and no models

names.answer: The reader wired for `the board` names `qwen3-vl-8b-instruct`, which does not take image. The board asked to save `qwen3-vl-8b-instruct` as its reader. The wiring names a model that cannot read what the request carries.
names.why: a model the board knows but cannot call this second is still a name with facts: the rule asks what the board knows, not what a client can call now, and the promise is read from `ModelKind` — the `vl` in the name says nothing. The answer is the model's promise, not `unknown` The words name the board, not a pool: the reader is the board's fact, and the door names no pool.

names.answer: The reader wired for `the board` names `gpt-9-mira`, which the caravan does not know. The board asked to save `gpt-9-mira` as its reader. A wiring that cannot be checked is not a path that reads.
names.why: the negative case for the reading: `unknown` is the answer for a name no place in the reading has, and this is the only case that can say it — a board with nothing to name. With the pools alone, every model name was answered this way, and the table could not tell a name the caravan does not know from a reading that does not look at models The words name the board, not a pool: the reader is the board's fact, and the door names no pool.
the absence named at the door: the reading is not asked about an empty name, and writing nothing is clearing a wiring, not a decision that reads nothing
